name: ReProver (LeanDojo)
one_liner: A retrieval-augmented language model proposes the next Lean tactic, and best-first search runs each tactic in Lean to get new proof states.

loop.proposes: Lean tactics, from a language model that first retrieves relevant premises from the math library
loop.judged_by: The Lean environment, driven through LeanDojo, which runs each tactic and reports the new state or an error
loop.steers: Best-first search expands the most promising proof states and feeds each new state back to the tactic generator

headline_result: On the LeanDojo Benchmark test set, pass@1 is 51.2% (random split) and 26.3% (novel_premises split) with retrieval, versus 47.6% and 23.2% without retrieval and 29.0% and 7.4% for zero-shot GPT-4. Also 26.5% on miniF2F and 13.8% on ProofNet (pass@1, 10 minute wall-time limit per theorem).
caveat: Main experiments use Lean 3 (Lean 4 results are in an appendix not covered here). The tactic generator is trained once, offline, on extracted proofs; search results do not update its weights. The paper's claim is about open, cheap training (one GPU week), not top accuracy.
beyond_harness_note: A search algorithm drives the proof and calls the model for candidate tactics; Lean decides validity and the output proof needs no model to check.
generative_model: Retrieval-augmented transformer tactic generator, trained on LeanDojo data

sources.title: LeanDojo: Theorem Proving with Retrieval-Augmented Language Models

verification.notes: Report gave only a GitHub org page; the paper is arXiv:2306.15626 (2023-06-27), which I opened (abstract plus results via HTML). The draft says NeurIPS 2023; venue not confirmed by me. Numbers read from the paper's tables. The draft said 'Counts as the prover, not the benchmark': agreed, card is for ReProver; it passes the filter because best-first search over Lean states steers generation, though weights are not updated by it.
